title: The table lowered
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies (the trilogy ran in print in three papers)
logline: Wood lowers the drafting table to floor height so the dog can rest his chin on his foot. A strip about a wrench.

panels.composition: The garage. The drafting table, its legs telescoped, WOOD on his knees with a wrench at one leg. BARNABY in the bed under it, watching.

image.prompt: a man kneeling with a wrench at the leg of a drafting table in a garage studio, loosening it, an old dog watching from a bed beneath, quiet ink with a desaturated wash

panels.composition: The leg dropping. The table now a foot off the floor. The lamp clamped to it, its cone now on the floorboards.

image.prompt: close-up of a drafting table leg lowered so the tabletop sits a foot above the floorboards, a swing-arm lamp's light pooling on the floor

panels.composition: Wood sitting cross-legged at the lowered table, drawing. The dog, without being carried, moving from the bed to Wood's foot. Chin on it.

image.prompt: a man sitting cross-legged on the floor drawing at a lowered drafting table, an old dog resting its chin across his foot, lamp light, no words

panels.composition: The garage from the door. Everything at floor height now. The man, the dog, the lamp, the work. It looks like it was always this way.
props: the whole room at floor level

image.prompt: a garage studio seen from its doorway with the drafting table lowered nearly to the floor, a man sitting cross-legged at it drawing, an old dog's chin on his foot, a lamp's warm cone, everything brought down to the dog's height, no words

art.line: quiet; water bleeding over the ink edge to suggest rain and fading light
art.palette: desaturated wet-on-wet: raw umber, Payne's gray, Prussian blue, raw sienna
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for the Sundays

notes: The table lowered. From here the room is at the dog's height.
